newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate debt deals focus on gov't tax talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate debt deals focus on gov't tax talk.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond spreads were mostly flat on Tuesday as players focused on nearly $1.0 billion in trust preferred deals, traders said.

The issuance of the trust preferred deals precedes a hearing by the House Ways and Means Committee on Wednesday that will address the Clinton Administration's 1998 budget proposals, including the removal of the tax deductable status of trust preferred dividend payments.
Should the Administration's proposal be passed, fixed-income analysts said Wednesday could emerge as the date the new tax treatment would become effective.

"A lot of conservative issuers may say there is a chance tomorrow may be the effective date and therefore may not want to issue more securities, said Andrew Gilligan, fixed-income analyst at Bear, Stearns & Co.
At the same time, Gilligan noted some trust preferred issuers may ignore the possibility and that it was a toss up as to whether issuance would come to a halt.

Topping the slate, American General Corp issued $500 million capital securities by competitive bid in the private placement market. Morgan Stanley took the 49-year deal with a bid spread of 126.7 basis points, market sources said.
One market source said the securities were reoffered at a spread of 123 basis points over the curve, although other Street sources scoffed at the rich price.
Coincidentally, Standard & Poor's assigned an A-plus rating to the deal while placing it under review for possible downgrade citing the pending merger with USLIFE Corp.
Morgan Stanley declined to comment on the deal.

Elsewhere, TCI Communications Inc sold $300 million Ba3/BB-plus rated 9.65 percent 30-year capital securities to yield 275 basis points over the curve via co-lead managers Lehman Brothers and Merrill Lynch & Co.

"Accounts have a bias toward buying, but they think spreads are too tight and they're waiting for new issue product to put cash into," one industrials trader said, adding that new issues have been "dull and sporadic."
Turning to high-yielding issues, few prices reflected large movements despite a flurry of early session trade but one large New York firm called spreads marginally wider.

Michaels Stores 10-7/8 percent debt was one of those few, traders said, gaining 1-1/2 points to 103 on speculation of fourth quarter earnings. In February, chief executive officer Michael Rouleau warned the Q4 results would probably be at the lower end of expectations.
Michaels said it will report fourth quarter earnings on Wednesday after the market close.
Marvel Holdings Inc's "old" bonds traded higher before falling about 3/8 point near mid-session. The debt retraced those losses and closed at 22-1/2 bid, one trader said.
In the new issue market, Anvil Knitwear Inc issued $130 million 10-7/8 percent B3/B-plus rated 10-year senior notes at par via a Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities syndicate.
The T-bond closed down 14/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
